segments.text: Carolina, where to start with this one? Let's start by saying you are through to the finals of Wimbledon.
But there were such fine margins between going through to a final and going home.
When you are in a battle like that, do you have time to think or is it a battle of survival?
Thank you. First of all, it sounds really nice to be in a final.
Honestly, it was such a big fight. It was a rollercoaster. As you said, you're up and down.
In 10 seconds, you have a match point, then you match point down. It's no time to think,
but very nerve-wracking. I was, you know, I don't even know what I'm saying. I'm really
kind of shaking and trying to sink in, but the atmosphere here, indescribable.
Thank you everyone who came and supported us.
At times it wasn't just a battle on the court, we saw you holding your side and I
think everybody was getting quite nervous. First of all, are you okay because we
know how tough it's been for you over the years even to get back to this
point? Yeah, I'm okay, I'm okay, I just was trying to catch a breath, you know, but
no, I'm good, I'm good, yeah, I'm good. I think you're very good. People might not
realize, but this is actually the first time that you have been out on Centre
Court. I think you came down with your team last night to see what it was like
to get a photo. You've got the chance to get another photo on Saturday, but
Just tell us what it was like to to come out here for the very first time.
It's such a huge moment as well.
Yeah, you know, there is so many of us tennis players
and I don't think many of us get to play on this court.
And it's such a history of our sport and it's
yeah, incredible, very special moment.
We came here to warm up with Linda actually before before the semis.
And yeah, took a photo.
It's just nice moment to experience all of this.
and this this cord is beautiful. Well you get to do it all again on Saturday
because you are through to the finals here at Wimbledon. Put your hands together.
Thank you.
